candidates.title: Stellar atmospheric parameter estimation from spectra
candidates.scope_summary: Infer temperature gravity metallicity or abundance parameters from stellar spectra.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Classification and spectral synthesis share objects and vocabulary but have different outputs.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: Multiple viable stellar-parameter and abundance query formulations exist.
candidates.overlap_risk: Directly overlaps the W4/W5 stellar-parameter Research Query.
candidates.decision_reason: Scientifically viable but excluded to avoid reusing the most developed W4/W5 task boundary.

candidates.title: Stellar spectral classification
candidates.scope_summary: Assign stellar types or classes directly from spectra.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Parameter regression and generic object classification are close semantic neighbours.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: Many stable machine-learning and neural-network query variants exist.
candidates.overlap_risk: Directly overlaps the W4/W5 spectral-classification Research Query.
candidates.decision_reason: Strong literature exists, but retaining it would overrepresent an already-used W4/W5 task.

candidates.title: Generic astronomical spectral preprocessing
candidates.scope_summary: Apply machine learning to broad spectral preprocessing without a narrower restoration objective.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Denoising generation and downstream parameterization are frequent boundary neighbours.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: The generic preprocessing wording is unstable and returns heterogeneous tasks.
candidates.overlap_risk: Directly overlaps W4/W5 preprocessing and is broader than a reproducible Topic boundary.
candidates.decision_reason: Replaced by the narrower denoising Topic; generic preprocessing is both overlapping and poorly retrievable.

candidates.title: Spectroscopic galaxy redshift estimation
candidates.scope_summary: Predict galaxy redshift from spectroscopy rather than broadband photometry.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Photometric-redshift papers are abundant lexical and semantic hard negatives.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: Queries are possible but repeatedly dominated by photometric-redshift results.
candidates.overlap_risk: Shares object and modality with galaxy activity classification and a regression role with existing parameter estimation.
candidates.decision_reason: Excluded because public queries showed severe photometric contamination and added less diversity than galaxy activity classification.

candidates.title: Galaxy activity classification from optical spectra
candidates.scope_summary: Classify star-forming composite AGN and LINER regimes from spectral evidence.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Photometric AGN selection redshift estimation and line measurement lack the required output or modality.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: Activity-class and AGN/LINER query variants retrieve a small but concrete literature.
candidates.overlap_risk: Same classification family as transient typing but a different object and physical label space.
candidates.decision_reason: Clear object/modality/output boundary and direct recent public evidence justify inclusion despite a modest corpus.

candidates.title: Quasar spectral classification and redshift
candidates.scope_summary: Identify or characterize quasars using spectral information.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Photometric quasar selection and galaxy-QSO classification frequently omit direct spectral input.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: Broad queries are viable but mix spectroscopy photometry classification and redshift tasks.
candidates.overlap_risk: The combined task is internally heterogeneous and overlaps galaxy activity classification.
candidates.decision_reason: Excluded because a single stable target task could not be frozen without narrowing beyond the gathered evidence.

candidates.title: Supernova spectral typing
candidates.scope_summary: Assign transient types from spectra including low-signal and phase-varying cases.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Photometric light-curve classification host identification and spectral generation are strong boundaries.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: Deep-learning and automated spectral-typing queries return direct methods such as DASH.
candidates.overlap_risk: Classification repeats a task family but adds a time-dependent transient object and modality.
candidates.decision_reason: Strong direct evidence and unusually clear photometry-versus-spectroscopy boundary support inclusion.

candidates.title: Exoplanet atmospheric retrieval from spectra
candidates.scope_summary: Infer atmospheric composition clouds and physical parameters from exoplanet spectra.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Light-curve detection forward spectrum generation and molecule detection without retrieval are close boundaries.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: Transmission/emission and neural/Bayesian retrieval variants retrieve direct literature.
candidates.overlap_risk: A regression/inference role is shared with stellar parameters, but object physics and modality differ substantially.
candidates.decision_reason: Distinct object and modality, strong direct evidence, and explicit forward-versus-inverse boundary justify inclusion.

candidates.title: Data-driven stellar radial velocity estimation
candidates.method_role: primary Doppler estimator or variability disentangler
candidates.scope_summary: Estimate stellar line-of-sight velocity from spectral shifts and variability.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Atmospheric parameter estimation classification and activity prediction share spectral vocabulary but not the output.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: Data-driven time-series and Doppler queries retrieve direct work including wobble.
candidates.overlap_risk: Uses stellar spectra like W4, but the physical output and time-series modality are distinct.
candidates.decision_reason: Retained as a distinct measurement problem with strong object/task hard negatives and adequate evidence.

candidates.title: Anomaly discovery in spectroscopic surveys
candidates.data_modality: large optical or infrared spectral surveys
candidates.method_role: primary novelty representation or anomaly score
candidates.scope_summary: Rank unusual spectra for scientific inspection beyond fixed known classes.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Rare-class supervised classifiers and non-spectral anomaly catalogues provide realistic negatives.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: Anomaly outlier and rare-object formulations retrieve complementary evidence.
candidates.overlap_risk: Broad object scope is intentional but constrained by a single discovery task and direct spectral input.
candidates.decision_reason: Adds unsupervised discovery and survey-scale diversity with a defensible supervised-versus-anomaly boundary.

candidates.title: Learned stellar spectral denoising
candidates.scope_summary: Restore spectral quality while preserving line profiles and downstream measurements.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Normalization parameter inference and synthetic generation are close but scientifically different roles.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: A broader query was too strict, while neural-network stellar denoising retrieved direct methods.
candidates.overlap_risk: Adjacent to W4 preprocessing, but narrower and explicitly evaluated as restoration rather than generic preprocessing.
candidates.decision_reason: The narrower boundary directly addresses W5 preprocessing-versus-parameterization errors without duplicating generic preprocessing.

candidates.title: Emission-line detection and deblending
candidates.scope_summary: Detect or separate spectral emission features using deep learning.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Strong-lens searches activity classification and anomaly detection can all depend on emission lines.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: The strict query returned no hits and a relaxed query mixed several downstream tasks.
candidates.overlap_risk: Task identity was not stable across retrieved examples and overlaps galaxy activity and anomaly Topics.
candidates.decision_reason: Excluded because the viability search did not isolate a sufficiently coherent learned deblending literature.

candidates.title: Learned telluric correction
candidates.scope_summary: Remove terrestrial atmospheric absorption from astronomical spectra.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: General instrument modelling exoplanet analysis and classical correction methods are close boundaries.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: Only four broad hits appeared and direct learned-correction evidence was sparse.
candidates.overlap_risk: Would add preprocessing diversity but evidence is thinner than the denoising Topic.
candidates.decision_reason: Excluded on literature viability and query precision rather than to reach a target Topic count.

candidates.title: Stellar spectral interpolation and emulation
candidates.scope_summary: Generate stellar spectra from physical parameters rather than infer parameters from observations.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Inverse parameterization denoising and normalization use the same words but reverse the method role.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: Interpolation and neural spectral-synthesis formulations retrieve direct work.
candidates.overlap_risk: Shares stellar vocabulary with several Topics but has a uniquely forward generative role.
candidates.decision_reason: Directly operationalizes the W5 generation-versus-preprocessing boundary and has adequate public evidence.

candidates.title: Solar spectropolarimetric inversion
candidates.scope_summary: Infer magnetic fields and atmospheric stratification from Stokes spectra.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: Solar image classification forward radiative transfer and non-solar parameter estimation are clear negatives.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: Spectropolarimetric and Stokes-profile formulations retrieve multiple direct neural inversion papers.
candidates.overlap_risk: An inverse task resembles parameter estimation, but spectropolarimetry and solar physics add real modality/object diversity.
candidates.decision_reason: Strong direct evidence and a distinctive polarized spectral modality justify inclusion.

candidates.title: 21-cm foreground removal
candidates.method_role: primary learned separator or restoration model
candidates.scope_summary: Recover cosmological 21-cm structure from spectrally resolved foreground contamination.
candidates.hard_negative_potential: RFI classification parameter inference HII-region identification and continuum imaging provide distinct boundaries.
candidates.query_variant_feasibility: The term 21cm is indexing-sensitive, but alternate formulations retrieve deep21 and related work.
candidates.overlap_risk: Low overlap with optical Topics; the main risk is mixing spectral cubes with non-spectral radio imaging.
candidates.decision_reason: Retained to add radio/cosmology modality diversity after alternate queries found direct foreground-removal work.

freeze_decision.decision_rule: Select only candidates with a coherent scientific object/modality/task/method-role boundary, at least one reproducible public viability query with direct evidence, useful hard negatives, and non-redundant coverage relative to W4/W5 and the new roster; no target count is enforced.

alternatives_considered: deterministic seeded random topic split: reproducible but can cluster objects or tasks on one side
manual object-only stratification: balances objects but can leave target-task families unbalanced
constrained balanced topic split: selected because it balances object modality task and method role without labels
split_decision.decision_rule: Allocate whole Topics only; keep approximately half hidden; balance scientific objects, optical/non-optical modalities, and classification/inference/preprocessing/generation task roles using frozen Topic metadata only, then resolve equally valid assignments by the recorded seed.
split_decision.custodian_policy: Hidden labels remain outside the ordinary repository under an independent custodian; the public repository may contain only a sealed external hash anchor and no reveal path.
